raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"Settle in.","source_id":"GLUE_PACING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"You're starting in Le Marais.","source_id":"SYNTHESIZED_OPENER","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"When you're ready, Place de la Bastille is about a twelve-minute walk from here.","source_id":"SYNTHESIZED_OPENER","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"As you come up Rue St. Antoine toward the square, keep your eyes on the pavement — something's been traced into the stones there, and I'll tell you what once we arrive.","source_id":"GLUE_STAGING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"It's July 1789, and revolution is stirring in the streets of Paris.","source_id":"b41ff2b7-8c00-48bf-973a-1797225b9e6b","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"The king's troops had abandoned the city center and fallen back on their one remaining stronghold in Paris — a castle-like fortress guarding the eastern edge of town, the Bastille.","source_id":"b41ff2b7-8c00-48bf-973a-1797225b9e6b","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"That fortress was a massive medieval castle, raised to defend the Paris of Charles V — thirteen years in the building, finished in 1382 — and the faubourg around it, the district that once lay outside the old city, still keeps a flavour of the past in its narrow streets.","source_id":"63e2ed73-7697-42ce-8f19-16b049a8a4c7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"By 1789 it doubled as a prison, and it had become the very symbol of royal oppression.","source_id":"b41ff2b7-8c00-48bf-973a-1797225b9e6b","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"But here's what the crowd got wrong: it was far from the grim dungeon everyone pictured.","source_id":"18966695-892a-42d7-9635-c88fe25a4f20","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"It ran more like a luxury prison for the well-connected.","source_id":"18966695-892a-42d7-9635-c88fe25a4f20","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Voltaire finished his tragedy Oedipe inside these walls, composing verses and dining well, and the notorious Marquis de Sade — held here that very year — draped his cell in fabric and had his own furniture moved in.","source_id":"18966695-892a-42d7-9635-c88fe25a4f20","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0,"also_cites":["b41ff2b7-8c00-48bf-973a-1797225b9e6b"]},{"text":"On the fourteenth of July, the people of Paris massed at the main gate and demanded the troops surrender.","source_id":"b41ff2b7-8c00-48bf-973a-1797225b9e6b","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Negotiations failed, so they stormed it.","source_id":"b41ff2b7-8c00-48bf-973a-1797225b9e6b","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Inside, the liberators found seven prisoners — seven — a far cry from the hundreds they'd imagined setting free.","source_id":"18966695-892a-42d7-9635-c88fe25a4f20","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0,"also_cites":["b41ff2b7-8c00-48bf-973a-1797225b9e6b"]},{"text":"For good measure, they mounted the heads of a few officials on their pikes.","source_id":"b41ff2b7-8c00-48bf-973a-1797225b9e6b","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"This triumph of citizens over their king lit a fire across all of France and set the Revolution going.","source_id":"b41ff2b7-8c00-48bf-973a-1797225b9e6b","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"A fortress that had taken years to raise came down in just four months, pulled apart brick by brick.","source_id":"63e2ed73-7697-42ce-8f19-16b049a8a4c7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0,"also_cites":["b41ff2b7-8c00-48bf-973a-1797225b9e6b"]},{"text":"And now all that's left is that faint outline in the pavement of Rue St. Antoine — the round turrets of the Bastille traced in cobblestones, about thirty yards before you reach the square.","source_id":"b41ff2b7-8c00-48bf-973a-1797225b9e6b","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Now lift your eyes to the tall column at the center of the square, topped by a gilded Liberty carrying the torch of freedom into the future — a monument to France's long struggle to build a democracy.","source_id":"ffd820d1-f959-4816-b18e-ecf30557a7ed","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"It doesn't mark 1789 at all, but a second uprising in 1830, when the conservative Charles X — who'd apparently forgotten the Revolution his own generation lived through — had to be tossed out.","source_id":"ffd820d1-f959-4816-b18e-ecf30557a7ed","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Through the unrest of the mid-1800s this square kept drawing worker rallies, and there were times the working class barricaded the streets of Paris — the very world Victor Hugo put on the page in Les Misérables.","source_id":"ffd820d1-f959-4816-b18e-ecf30557a7ed","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"It still draws demonstrations today, and every fourteenth of July the whole country remembers the day the Bastille fell — Bastille Day, France's national holiday.","source_id":"ffd820d1-f959-4816-b18e-ecf30557a7ed","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0}]}
